newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - Brazilian spreads ease.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - Brazilian spreads ease.

text.p: Cash spreads on Brazilian coffees softened this week, while differentials on other grades held firm despite the rising futures market, traders said.
"Only Brazil is very competitive," one trader said. "It is difficult to get offers on anything else from anybody."

Traders said the pressure of the upcoming Brazilian harvest season -- which is starting now but will begin in earnest in June -- and growers' desire to take advantage of attractively high futures prices caused differentials from the world's top producer to head lower.

Spot Brazil Santos 4s were heard at 10 cents under "C", down some two cents from week-ago levels. Santos 2/3s, also for spot delivery, were offered at four cents under "C" compared with even to two cents over last week.
"Brazils are selling like hotcakes," a trader said, "because there is nothing else."

Other coffees were not only hard to come by, traders said, but priced too high to tempt buyers. With most roasters' near-term requirements taken care of, traders said sky-high spot differentials and May's hefty premium to second-month July discouraged prompt business.
"For April, May and June, roasters are out of the market," one dealer said. "We're seeing some odds and ends and some price-fixing, but producers still want to price against May."
Traders said roasters were trying to concentrate on forward delivery, but uncertainty ahead of the upcoming Brazilian frost season in June through August made producers reluctant sellers.
"Producers are not going to aggressively sell what they have left ahead of the (Brazil) frost season," a trader said.

Additionally, nearby Colombian coffees were virtually unavailable, with no offers through July, after the country's National Coffee Growers' Federation announcing last week that it was closing registrations for May/June shipments.
Differentials on spot Colombian MAMs held steady at a pricey 30 cents over the CSCE May contract.
CSCE May coffee fell 3.40 cents a lb Friday to settle at 216.35. July ended 4.95 lower at 193.25.
